# jochwacht-sbom 0.12.0 — embtrace is now Jochwacht

Same tool, same code line, new name. `embtrace` collided with a registered
trademark, so the product family is now **Jochwacht** (DPMA 302026254573.4).
Nothing about what the tool does, reads or sends has changed.

## What you need to do

Nothing, unless you want to. The old commands and the old packages keep
working.

```bash
pipx install jochwacht-sbom
jochwacht-sbom .                 # writes sbom.cdx.json, sends nothing
```

## What keeps working

| You have | What happens |
|---|---|
| `embtrace-sbom` / `embtrace-check` on the command line | one line of notice on stderr, then the same tool |
| `pip install embtrace-sbom` / `embtrace-check` | installs `jochwacht-sbom` and keeps the command |
| `import embtrace_sbom.…` in a script | resolves to the same modules |
| `except EmbtraceError` in a script | same object as `JochwachtError` |
| `EMBTRACE_SBOM_TRACEBACK`, `EMBTRACE_NO_SYSRESOLVE` | still read; `JOCHWACHT_*` wins when both are set |
| `.embtraceignore`, `embtrace-deps.yaml`, `embtrace.yaml` | unchanged — the suite reads the same names |

The notice goes to **stderr**, so a pipeline that reads `stdout` is
unaffected.

## What did change

- The default submission address is now `https://api.jochwacht.dev`. The
  old host keeps answering, so an older collector you have installed
  somewhere does not break.
- Links point at `jochwacht.dev`.
- The old distribution names `embtrace-sbom`, `embtrace-check` and
  `embtrace` receive one final version each that says where the tool went,
  and are then yanked — never deleted, so nothing that pins them breaks.

Licence unchanged: GPL-3.0-or-later (releases up to embtrace-check 0.8.6
stay MIT).
